segments.text: It is false. For, I. there is not the least thing in nature, but it commeth to passe by the decree and will of God. Math. 10.30. Wherefore such as affirme, that God did onely foreknow this, or that, they doe either quite ouerturne the prouidence of GOD, or at the least imagine that it is a very idle prouidence. II. The fact of Herod and Pilate in deliuering Christ against their own consciences, to be crucified, may seeme to be as heinous as was Adams fall, and yet they are said to haue done that, which the hand of the Lord had fore-ordained to be done. Act. 4. 28. Againe, the fall of Adam was two manner of waies by Gods actiue, or rather operatiue permission. I. In as much as the fall was an action: for in God alone we liue, we mooue, and haue our beeing. II. In as much as that his fall was but a bare triall of his loyaltie to God, whereby God would trie both the power, and will of his creature.
